as_told.title: Remote viewing program with Puthoff, Targ and Pat Price

plain: Remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe distant places or hidden things using only the mind, is said to have grown into a US government programme between the 1960s and 1970s through the physicists Hal Puthoff and Russell Targ and an artist and psychic named Ingo Swann. A former Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan, who later joined the unit, tells Michels that they brought in Swann, that Swann worked out a method called controlled remote viewing, and that the remote viewing unit had already existed for ten years when he got there. Dan Sheehan, speaking as a researcher, links Puthoff and Targ to what he calls the entire psychic programme, but names a psychic called Pat Price rather than Swann. Neither gives a source. If true, it would mean the US government spent years trying to use psychics for intelligence work.
